# Verify

> Verify (@revyl/verify) is an open-source TypeScript library for Revyl. It opens cloud browsers and iOS/Android devices for agent instruction/validation/extract steps, or Mac computers for commands, files, processes, screenshots, clicks and keys on the screen, checks answered by the Mac's own vision model, and the private screen recording after close. Call it from a plain script, coding agent, CI, or any test runner. It has no test runner of its own.

## Docs

Mac computers are available to organizations on a current paid Revyl plan. See computers.md#availability-and-errors.

- [Getting started](getting-started.md): install, authenticate, init, run a script
- [API](api.md): open() and session profiles (Revyl runs a profile from .revyl/config.yaml before open() returns; profile plus sessionProfileProjectId reads it from the project's default branch in Git without a local config, script or branch; the project ID must be a UUID and profile must be a name, not empty or 'none'), attach(), hosted children, navigate(), cdp() for Playwright and Puppeteer on web, report(), agent steps, extract(), screenshot(), exec(), file/process methods, close(), persistent computers

- [Computers](computers.md#availability-and-errors): Mac availability, commands and files, the screen (clicks, typing and keys), validation() and extract() on a Mac opened with inference, app sessions inside a Mac, persistent computers, expiry, capacity errors, recording metadata, and confirmed release

## Session profiles

For an implicit checkout session.default_profile on web, iOS or Android, Verify checks GET /api/v1/backend-capabilities?contract=session_profile_starts. The device_session_session_profile_picks capability switches the request from named to default with the same name, checkout files and source, so Revyl can skip defaults for untargeted apps. A missing capability or failed read preserves named. Explicit profiles and Mac computer defaults always send named without this read.

## Exact actions and coordinates

Prefer a description, such as `tap({ target: 'Sign in button' })`: Revyl finds the element on the current screen, and you never handle coordinates. Otherwise a point is `{ x, y }` in screenshot pixels on every platform: whole numbers from the top-left corner of the image `screenshot()` returns. So a position you read off a screenshot goes to `tap()`, `type()`, `swipe()` and every other exact action unchanged. `screenSize()` returns the screenshot's width and height, and `locate()` and the points `tap()`, `doubleTap()`, `longPress()` and `type()` return use the same pixels. A point outside the screenshot is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any action is sent, and the message names the valid range. On iOS, Verify converts the pixels to the screen's points for you. On Web they equal CSS pixels at the default device scale factor of 1, and you still pass screenshot pixels at any other. This holds from TypeScript 0.4.1, Python 0.2.1 and Go v0.3.1; earlier versions took iOS points. On a Mac computer a point is in screenshot pixels too, and `tap({ target })` returns the point it clicked in the same pixels. Verify refuses a negative or fractional point before sending it, and Revyl refuses one past the screen's edge without clicking; both throw `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the valid range. See [For coding agents](agents.md#exact-actions-and-coordinates) for a runnable example.

Exact actions are `tap`, `doubleTap`, `longPress`, `type`, `swipe`, `drag`, `pressKey`, `locate` and `screenSize` on Web, iOS and Android. Web adds `typeFocused(text)`, which types into the field that has focus, and `pressKey` keys such as `'escape'`, `'tab'` and arrows with `modifiers`. iOS and Android add `goHome()`; their `pressKey` takes only `'enter'` and `'backspace'`. To type on every platform, use `type({ target: 'Email field' }, text)`, which taps the field and types into it; `typeFocused` on Web with no field focused throws `ACTION_FAILED` (reason `no_focused_input`), and on iOS and Android it throws `NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM`. A Mac computer's screen takes `tap({ x, y })`, `tap({ target })` (which returns the point it clicked; check it, because grounding can click a look-alike or something else when the target isn't there), `type({ target }, text)`, `screenSize()`, `typeFocused(text, { clear: false })` and `pressKey` with the Web keys, where `'meta'` is Command: select all with `pressKey('a', { modifiers: ['meta'] })` there and `pressKey('a', { modifiers: ['ctrl'] })` on Web. See [computers.md](computers.md#screen). A call the platform lacks throws `NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM` before anything is sent, naming what to use instead. See [api.md](api.md#exact-actions) for every call.

On Web the browser runtime waits after each `tap`, `doubleTap`, `longPress`, `type`, `typeFocused`, `swipe`, `drag` and `pressKey` until the page stops changing, up to about 6 seconds, and a game or animation never stops. Pass `{ settle: false }` for games, animations and rapid input such as `pressKey('arrowleft', { settle: false })` every few hundred milliseconds: the call returns as soon as the input is sent, before the screen may have changed, so take a `screenshot()` or run a `validation()` when you need to see the result, and don't rely on the next screenshot showing it. iOS, Android and Mac computers don't wait, so `settle: false` changes nothing there. Python takes `settle=False` and Go `Settle: new(false)`. See [api.md](api.md#exact-actions).
